name: core.openwop.workflows.campaign-journeys
description: Contact-level lifecycle journeys as RFC 0013 chains on the ONE engine (ADR 0222 / campaign gap plan C6) — NOT a journey engine. Trigger with an ADR 0208 host-event binding (e.g. host.crm.contact.created → Welcome Series), guard with the enrollment + eligibility verbs (one run per contact per journey; every send behind consent + suppression), wait with core.flow.wait, send with the existing email node, log with the CRM activity verb. Enrollment state is the run itself — monitor in Runs, reset re-enrollment via the campaign-journeys API.
author: openwop

chains.label: Welcome Series (2-step)
chains.description: New contact → welcome email → wait a day → follow-up email. ONE sign-off gate covers BOTH sends, and covering both is structural rather than a promise: the welcome send is reachable ONLY through `recheck`, which runs solely on the gate's `truthy approved` edge, so a rejection skips the welcome, which skips the wait, the re-check and the follow-up in turn (WF-EM-3 — the follow-up deliberately carries no second gate; a day-later interrupt would strand the run and contradict the hands-off operation this gate advertises). The RECIPIENT ADDRESS never rides the gate: the approver SEES it (`gate1.email` is the gate's read-only artifact), but the address BOUND to the send comes from `recheck` — a second `feature.campaign-journeys.nodes.eligibility` evaluation downstream of the approval — so an approver cannot redirect the mail by editing the artifact, and consent + suppression are re-evaluated at the moment of approval rather than whenever the gate was raised. The day-2 re-check is that same compliance gate one wait later: it FAILS on revoked consent or a suppression added during the wait, and a failed upstream blocks the follow-up. Bind it to host.crm.contact.created (the contact rides the event payload), or run it manually with a contactId. The enrollment guard makes redelivered events harmless; every send passes consent + suppression first.

config.title: Start the welcome series for this contact?
config.prompt: Two emails will be sent (welcome now, follow-up in a day) to the address shown. Rejecting stops BOTH — the follow-up is downstream of the welcome, so it is never reached. The address is shown for REVIEW ONLY: it is re-resolved from the contact after approval, so editing it here changes nothing. Approval policies can auto-clear this gate for hands-off operation.

chains.label: Re-engage a Contact
chains.description: One quiet contact → human sign-off → re-engagement email + a CRM follow-up task. The RECIPIENT ADDRESS never rides the gate: the approver sees `gate.email` as a read-only artifact, but the address bound to the send comes from `recheck`, a second eligibility evaluation downstream of the approval — so an approver cannot redirect the mail by editing the artifact, and consent + suppression are re-evaluated at the moment of approval. Rejecting skips `recheck`, which skips the send and the task in turn. Run it manually, from the Strategist in chat, or bind it to an event carrying a contactId. Segment-wide sweeps are the recorded follow-on (they need per-member fan-out).

orgId.description: The CRM org that owns the follow-up task.

body.default: It has been a while — here is what changed since your last visit.

senderEmail.description: Verified sender address these emails are sent from.

config.title: Re-engage this contact?
config.prompt: A re-engagement email will be sent to the address shown. Rejecting sends nothing and creates no follow-up task. The address is shown for REVIEW ONLY: it is re-resolved from the contact after approval, so editing it here changes nothing.

chains.label: Segment Winback (per-member fan-out)
chains.description: One quiet SEGMENT → resolve its members (capped) → a data-driven supervisor fans ONE re-engagement child workflow out over every member, each child receiving its OWN contactId (RFC 0126 per-item input on core.dispatch, ADR 0255). This is the segment-wide sweep the single-contact `re-engage-contact` chain deferred (its own description: 'Segment-wide sweeps are the recorded follow-on — they need per-member fan-out'). WIRING: install `campaign-journeys.re-engage-contact` FIRST in DEFERRED mode (`POST /workflows/from-chain {chainId, deferred:true}`) so each fanned child binds its own contactId + shared params per run rather than a frozen one, then pass that returned workflowId as `childWorkflowId`. Every per-member child still runs the full enroll-guard + consent/suppression + sign-off + send + follow-up-task path; idempotent by the child enroll-CAS, so a re-swept segment never double-sends. Bounded by the segment-members cap (5000) and the host fan-out cap. Run it with a `segmentId` (the segment rides the run inputs).

childWorkflowId.description: The installed re-engage-contact workflow id (e.g. `wf.campaign-journeys-re-engage-contact.<hash>`) each member fans out to. Install `campaign-journeys.re-engage-contact` in DEFERRED mode first (so the per-member contactId + shared params bind per child run, not a frozen value) and paste its returned workflowId here.

fromAddress.description: The verified sender address, forwarded to every per-member child.

orgId.description: The CRM org that owns each member's follow-up task, forwarded to every child.

subject.description: Re-engagement subject, shared across the whole segment.

body.default: It has been a while — here is what changed since your last visit.
body.description: Re-engagement body, shared across the whole segment.

nodes.name: Fan out one re-engage child per member

dispatched.description: The number of per-member re-engage children fanned out (0 for an empty segment).
